A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ABMILX research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and repagination in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original pathology benchmark experiments, computational-cost measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses across PANDA, TCGA, and CAMELYON.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds CPTAC external-validation results, expanded baseline results, and an empirical optimization-risk analysis.

M1.justification: The multi-scale random sampling, multi-head local attention, global attention-plus module, and training objective remain unchanged in Section 3 and Equations 1–5. The new MAX-N statistic is used for evaluation.

E1.justification: v2 adds CPTAC-LUAD and CPTAC-LUSC as external cohorts, reporting NSCLC subtyping and LUAD survival evaluation in Table 3. This substantially extends coverage to cross-dataset transfer while retaining the original pathology datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add 2DMamba comparisons using CHIEF, UNI, and GigaPath features and expand RRTMIL comparisons. These aggregator families already appeared with ResNet, and v1 Appendix Table 4 already summarized some FM-based RRT results; the change expands comparator combinations within the existing method families.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an external evaluation design using TCGA-trained models on CPTAC, substantially extending the original within-dataset evaluations. Appendix A.4 also introduces MAX-N measurement during early E2E training. Existing splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New CPTAC testing examines robustness to cross-dataset domain shifts. Appendix A.4 additionally tests the proposed risk mechanism quantitatively: Table 5 reports MAX-N of 21.2162 for ABMIL versus 2.6557 for ABMILX. These add distinct robustness and mechanism analyses beyond the retained ablations and visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 1,000 bootstrap evaluations with means and 95% confidence intervals. Added baseline rows follow the existing reporting practice; Tables 3 and 5 provide point estimates. No new seed information, repeated-training counts, significance tests, or uncertainty procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported results, including CPTAC scores of 85.19 AUC and 54.00 C-index for ABMILX and 76.37 PANDA accuracy for UNI+2DMamba. Table 2 replaces ResNet-50+2DMamba survival OOM entries with 61.41, 61.94, and 54.98. MAX-N results are also added; the original ABMILX benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces the nonstandard mathematical definition of MAX-N: maximum noisy-instance attention multiplied by the number of instances. The original optimization-risk definition, assumptions, and derivations in Equations 6–33 remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about sparse-attention optimization difficulties, ABMILX’s mitigation mechanism, and computationally efficient E2E performance competitive with foundation models.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets CPTAC results as demonstrating robust transferability across domain shifts. Appendix A.4 interprets reduced MAX-N as validating the risk mechanism and explaining performance gains. These extend the scientific interpretation, while the limitations in Appendix F remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly identifies BRCA explicitly as the survival-ablation dataset. Other settings repeated there, including the ResNet-18 encoder and inference input size, were already documented in v1 Appendix B.3. Implementation hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and brief positioning relative to general high-resolution E2E vision methods and recent MIL work, removes the CAMIL citation, and changes the introductory attribution of the two-stage paradigm from Lu et al. to Campanella et al. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and cross-reference edits, adds an appendix contents page and subsection headings, and updates affiliations, publication status, and acknowledgements. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain additional rows, and new Tables 3 and 5 display external-validation and risk-analysis results. Existing tables are renumbered and reflowed, and appendix figures move with pagination. Figures 1–6 retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: Expanded foundation-model comparisons, CPTAC validation, and the MAX-N analysis provide useful evidence absent from v1. The gain is limited by missing CPTAC cohort details and uncertainty estimates, plus overstated superiority over UNI: Table 3 reports 85.19 AUC for ABMILX versus 85.24 for UNI+TransMIL. The additions improve assessability despite these reporting and interpretation shortcomings.
